plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding, white bell-shaped flowers push up through frost, leaf litter and sometimes snow. Each bloom has three long outer petals and a smaller inner ring marked with a green notch. They carpet woodlands, churchyards and old gardens in drifts, and they are often the first sign that winter is loosening its grip.
plants.bloomingSeason: Typically January to February, and sometimes earlier in mild winters
plants.location: Woodlands and gardens across the United Kingdom
plants.funFact: Snowdrops make natural antifreeze-like proteins that help their tissues cope with cold. Their compound galantamine has also been developed into a medicine used for early-stage Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Prunus campanulata
plants.description: Drooping, bell-shaped flowers in deep rosy pink hang along bare branches and glow against green hillsides. They open weeks or months before the pale cherry blossoms of mainland Japan. Okinawa's blossom-viewing season starts while much of the country is still in winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-January to mid-February, with the peak from late January to early February
plants.funFact: This cherry blooms in the opposite direction from most Japanese cherries. Okinawa's blossoms open first in the cooler northern hills and move south, so the bloom front travels from north to south.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.commonName: Agapanthus (African Lily, Lily of the Nile)
plants.description: Round clusters of funnel-shaped, sky-blue flowers sit on tall, sturdy stalks above arching, strap-like leaves. In the Southern Hemisphere summer they line driveways, coastal paths and sunny borders with waves of blue. They are a favorite with bees and with gardeners who want little fuss.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, mainly November to February
plants.location: Gardens and coastal areas of southern Australia and New Zealand, originally from South Africa
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Greek words for love and flower. Despite the common name Lily of the Nile, the plant is native to South Africa and is not a true lily. Its flowers open on tall stalks that can reach about a meter.
